messages:
Ivy R: Quick sync — proposing an audit-loop based canary design where local observers can make fast bailout decisions but all promotions require a central audit token. Aim: keep per-tenant fairness and let heavy tenants opt-in to stricter fallbacks.

Ravi S: Sounds reasonable. Two clarifications: what grants an observer the right to route traffic away (fast path) vs when must it consult central auditor?

Ivy R: Rule of thumb: observers can do temporary hedges for <= 30s using local signals (error spike, kernel OOM). Any sustained action > 30s needs an audit token from controller. Audit token is lease-based and short lived.

Tom H: How do we avoid noisy neighbors? If tenant A floods errors, we shouldn't penalize tenant B. Need per-tenant signal aggregation and isolation.

Jin: Per-tenant isolation is critical. Proposal: maintain a policy table keyed by tenant-id with fields: fallback_preference [cache|quant|hosted], max_spill_pct, emergency_cutoff. Controller merges cluster-level and tenant-level policies.

ops-bot: deploy 2901123456: rollout started for variant "v3-fast" to 1% traffic. Monitoring rules loaded.

Priya: On cache/kv warming — mirror 0.2% to the new variant and also shadow the kernel warmup sequence. Mirror stream should skip expensive ops (e.g., long generation) to avoid cost blowup.

Ravi S: We need a clear hierarchy of fallbacks. My suggestion: 1) local cache lookup (prefix) 2) sticky pin to tenant's last-known-good variant 3) quantized variant 4) upstream hosted fallback. Each step records a distinct telemetry tag.

Ivy R: Agree. Also require token compatibility across variants — the router should be able to map auth tokens -> tenant policy so we can do tenant-aware decisions without leaking identities to central controller.

Tom H: What about split-brain during network partition? If controller unreachable, observers must continue limited operation. Suggest: allow "degraded mode" with reduced spill percentages and disable promotions to STABLE.

Jin: Telemetry contract idea: every route decision emits fields: tenant, variant_from, variant_to, reason_code, signal_weights (latency:0.4,error:0.35,quality:0.25), cache_hit. We'll also emit a small representative output hash to detect drift without leaking content.

Priya: Example PromQL for canary latency alert: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{variant="v3-fast"}[5m])) by (le)) > (0.9 * SLA_seconds)
```
But need to bind by tenant for per-tenant alerts.

Ivy R: State machine sketch: INIT -> SHADOW (mirror only) -> CANARY (low traffic) -> RAMP (gradual increase) -> STABLE. Emergency transitions: any -> ROLLBACK or EMERGENCY_SPILL. Observers may trigger EMERGENCY_SPILL locally; controller confirms and persists.

Ravi S: Add cooldown windows to avoid flip-flopping: after an observer-triggered spill, block promotions for X minutes and require additional audit if behavior resumes.

Tom H: Ops playbook snippet: on EMERGENCY_SPILL: 1) route affected tenants to pinned variant 2) scale down new variant to zero 3) capture a snapshot of cache keys and recent traces 4) notify oncall with tenant impact list.

Priya: Testing: run chaos job that kills controller and simulates high-latency between regions, validate degraded mode constraints. Also simulate stale-cache where shadow warming doesn't happen and measure cold-start tail.

Jin: One more safety: automated canary quality checks — replay a curated eval set through both variants every 10m, compute a compact score, and if quality_delta < -threshold mark as failing. This score should be part of the audit token decision.

Ivy R: Action items: Jin will draft telemetry fields and eval harness; Ravi will write the policy-table schema; Tom will add degraded-mode semantics to the runbook; Priya will prototype the mirror filter to limit cost. I'll assemble a short RFC follow-up with state machine + audit token flow.

Ravi S: No blockers from me.

Tom H: I'll schedule a 30m follow-up to review the RFC draft.

Ivy R: Thanks all. Marking this thread as input for the RFC doc. :white_check_mark:
